title: Priority-lane capacity matrix and launch mitigation playbook for runtime/console/api
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: create a single canonical Priority-Lane Capacity Matrix and an associated Launch Mitigation Playbook that product, runtime, console, and API teams use to plan release trains. This artifact should map launch cohorts to reserved capacity bands, define soft-freeze and hard-freeze windows per lane, and provide deterministic mitigation steps (fallback model variants, regional failover, throttle policies) for capacity or SLO regressions. Outcome: reduce last-mile coordination overhead, shorten decision latency during launch incidents, and provide a repeatable runbook for cross-team rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical matrix produced with lanes: Critical, High, Default, Low and mapped capacity buckets (baseline qps, burst headroom) for US/EU/APAC
Mitigation playbook documented with RACI, automated and manual rollback steps, and validated ownership for each action
Telemetry gates defined and wired to dashboards and alerting rules (grafana/datasource links included)
Two dry-run simulations run with runtime + console + api teams and lessons captured
Playbook and matrix reviewed and approved by Engineering, SRE, and Product leadership
rollout_timeline: Week 0 (2026-02-10 to 2026-02-16): Draft matrix + initial capacity profiles from Eng (ENG-4821 deliverables)
Week 1 (2026-02-17 to 2026-02-23): Cross-functional review sessions + incorporate console and API constraints
Week 2 (2026-02-24 to 2026-03-01): Telemetry gating wiring and alert thresholds set; SRE approves alerting
Week 3 (2026-03-02 to 2026-03-08): Dry-run 1 (canary cohort) — observe traffic shaping and fallback behavior
Week 4 (2026-03-09 to 2026-03-15): Dry-run 2 (regional failover) + finalize playbook and handoff to launch ops
mitigation_playbook: Tier 0 (Critical lane regressions): Immediate fallback to pre-approved model variant (owner: Runtime lead) and switch to reserved dedicated capacity pool; notify incident bridge
Tier 1 (High lane regressions): Apply prefix-based throttling at API gateway (owner: API Platform), reduce non-essential background workloads, enable KV-cache bypass where safe
Tier 2 (Default/Low): Auto-scale burst pools up to configured cap; if scaling fails, initiate rolling feature flag rollback via console rollout tool
Escalation matrix: SRE -> Runtime -> Product -> Customer Success; Slack channel #launch-ops and Pager duty rotations listed in runbook
Rollback criteria: 15-minute sustained token-latency > 2x baseline AND error-rate increase > 0.5% above baseline over 5m
telemetry_gates: Latency p95 and p99 per-lane (thresholds documented) wired to grafana panels
Error rate (5m) per-route above baseline -> auto-notify release owner
Token-per-request cost delta monitoring to avoid runaway spend during rollouts
Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/launch/launch-health ; runbook alert rules: https://alerts.redwood.ai/r/launch-lanes
updates: 2025-11-04: Created ticket; initial outline and ask to Eng for capacity profiles (ENG-4821).
2025-11-18: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. Action: Eng to provide steady-state qps and burst headroom per model variant.
2025-12-02: Runtime team provided draft capacity profiles. Noted variance on long-context models; need conservative headroom for KV-cache warmup.
2026-01-12: SRE requested explicit SLO rollback thresholds; added to playbook draft. Assigned alert wiring to SRE (ENG-5120).
2026-01-28: Design provided sketch for console rollout UI to select lane and apply mitigation (see design link).
2026-02-03: PM review with Launch Ops — agreed on four-lane taxonomy and naming convention. Decided against per-customer lanes for initial rollout (too complex).
2026-02-10: Matrix v0.1 posted to Confluence and shared with reviewers. Dry-run dates tentatively scheduled for Mar 2 and Mar 9.
Pending: schedule dry-run invites and confirm dedicated capacity reservations with Infra team.
decisions: Adopt four launch lanes (Critical/High/Default/Low) instead of a continuous spectrum to simplify ops playbook.
Use model-variant fallback as first-line mitigation for Critical lane issues; reserve Dedicated pool for Critical by default.
Console rollout will include explicit 'lane' selection and checklist to apply mitigation steps; UI spec owned by Design (Riley Torres).
notes: Keep the initial matrix conservative — better to reserve slightly more capacity for the first two launches and tighten after dry-run learnings.
We intentionally avoid tying lanes to customer tiers in v1; v2 can add customer-mapped guardrails if demand requires.
Reference: incident learnings from runtime-2025-11 (postmortem linked in Confluence) were used to derive rollback thresholds.
